data.title: Repeated A2A Payments at Maximum Per-Transaction Limit
data.description: Detects multiple account-to-account payments where each transaction is at or near the maximum per-transaction limit (e.g., $2,500 for Zelle, $500,000 for FedNow). Fraudsters often structure payments at the exact limit to maximize extraction speed while avoiding aggregate-amount alerts, a behavior rarely seen in legitimate consumer transactions.

enrichment_required.source: Payment rail enrichment (percentage of rail transaction limit)

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Repeated A2A Payments at Maximum Per-Transaction Limit")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: selection and filter_at_limit | count() by account_id > 3")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:a2a_processing
event_type="a2a_payment_initiated"
(payment_rail="ZELLE" OR payment_rail="FEDNOW" OR payment_rail="RTP" OR payment_rail="ACH_SAMEDAY")
amount_pct_of_rail_limit>=95
| stats count as event_count by account_id
| where event_count > 3

falsepositives: Customer making a large one-time purchase split across multiple payments at platform limits
Business account regularly transacting at high values for legitimate operations
